title: adaptive-coalescing-playbook-sprint-28
summary: Sprint 28 working notes for rollout of adaptive coalescing and cooldown backpressure. Covers daily standups, experiments, decision rationale, and a lightweight playbook for canarying the feature across Dedicated pools.
content:
Purpose: capture the week of engineering updates, experiment outcomes, and an operational playbook for shipping 'adaptive coalescing' — a change to our batching layer that dynamically merges short inflight requests to improve GPU amortization while respecting latency SLOs. This doc is intentionally informal: notes, TODOs, rough numbers.

Context (short):
- Problem: observed wasteful small micro-batches for many customer flows (chat tokens under 32) causing high per-token cost despite low p50 latency.
- Proposed: adaptive coalescing algorithm that delays servicing an initial request by up to X ms to wait for compatible requests (same model variant, same route, compatible temperature/stop tokens).
- SLO constraint: target p95 <= 650ms for interactive models; adjustments needed for constrained Dedicated p95 targets.

Week goals (Sprint 28):
1) Finalize core algorithm and kernel handshake for coalesced batches.
2) Run A/B across two Dedicated pools (canary) for 72 hours.
3) Add a cooldown/backpressure window to avoid oscillation on bursty traffic.
4) Instrument new metrics: coalesce_wait_ms, coalesce_size, coalesce_hit_ratio, post_coalesce_p95, kv-prefill-impact.

Day-by-day standup style notes:
- 2026-05-25 (Mon) — Kickoff
  - Quick sync with kernel team: agreed on handshake that includes kv-cache compatibility bit and kv-cache-seed-id so merged requests share the same KV addressing. (Liam + Sara)
  - Miguel's prototype kernel path showed 6% perf regression on 8k sequence on CUDA 13 due to extra memcpy; kernel PR pointed for micro-optimizations. (PR #659)
  - Open question: how to treat function-calling/tool-call requests that are not merge-safe. Decision: explicit opt-out via route header; default is opt-in.

- 2026-05-26 (Tue) — Experiment design
  - Diego drafted experiment: split pool A (baseline) vs pool B (adaptive coalesce enabled at 10ms max wait) for 72h. Metric owners assigned. (INF-3421)
  - Added cooldown heuristic: when coalesce_hit_ratio > 0.6 for 5m, gradually increase max-wait to 25ms; when backend p95 rises > +10% over baseline, revert and inject 60s cooldown.
  - Note: must coordinate with Console routing to set canary tag. Added a route flag: x-rdwd-coalesce=auto/canary/off.

- 2026-05-27 (Wed) — Midweek check-in + kernel fixes
  - Kernel micro-optimizations landed to avoid the memcpy penalty: swap buffer pooling + pre-allocated fused-IO path. PR #660. Early microbench: regained previous perf numbers on 8k seq.
  - Runbook item: disable coalescing for models where fused kernels are not available. We flagged 13 models in the catalog.
  - Experiment start delayed by 4h due to GPU maintenance in eu-west-1; rescheduled.

- 2026-05-28 (Thu) — Experiment results (first 24h)
  - Observed: coalesce_hit_ratio = 0.38 overall; median coalesce_size = 2; median coalesce_wait = 7ms.
  - Latency: pool B post_coalesce_p95 rose by 4% on interactive routes, but overall token cost dropped by ~9% for those routes.
  - Interesting: some low-traffic customers on Dedicated saw an increase in p95 due to queueing at ingress (per-route burstiness).
  - Action: add per-route quick-reject if per-route inflight > 150 requests to reduce added latency.

- 2026-05-29 (Fri) — Triage + playbook drafting
  - Triage meeting (SRE + Console + Eng): agreed on a two-stage rollout:
    1) Soft canary: enable adaptive coalescing on non-SLA interactive routes (flag: canary) with max-wait 8ms and per-route inflight ceiling 80. Monitor for 24h.
    2) If metrics look stable (p95 delta <= +5%), widen to more pools and raise max-wait to 15ms and test the cooldown window behavior.
  - Agreed operational alerts: coalesce_hit_ratio_up (>=0.5), post_coalesce_p95_inc (>=+10%), customer_p95_delta (>=+7%). Attach runbook to alert.

Key decisions made:
- Default mode: adaptive coalescing will be opt-in per route via x-rdwd-coalesce header. Console will default to 'off' for newly created routes to be conservative.
- Cooldown/backpressure: implement immediate rollback for a pool if post_coalesce_p95 inc > +15% sustained for 3m, and auto-backoff to 'off' for 60s.
- Kernel compatibility: do not enable for models without fused-kernel support; surface as model-attribute coalesce_compat.

Experiment metrics snapshot (72h target):
- Baseline (pool A): p50 tokens 18ms, p95 tokens 420ms, token cost $0.0032
- Coalesce (pool B, first 24h): p50 tokens 21ms, p95 tokens 438ms (+4%), token cost $0.0029 (-9%)
- coalesce_hit_ratio (first 24h): 0.38; expected 0.45 after tuning routing defaults
- median coalesce_wait: 7ms; target 10-15ms for better batching without hurting p95

Operational playbook (short):
- Pre-rollout checks:
  - Confirm model list marked coalesce_compat in model catalog.
  - Ensure PR #660 is deployed to all serving nodes in the pool.
  - Update Console toggles and alerting dashboards (Graphs: coalesce_hit_ratio, post_coalesce_p95, per-route inflight).
- Canary steps:
  1) Enable header-based canary for 5% of traffic or specific canary customers.
  2) Monitor core metrics for 24h. If anomalies, hit rollback toggle for the pool.
  3) If stable, bump canary slice to 25% and raise max-wait to 15ms for next 24h.
- Rollback & postmortem:
  - Rollback immediate if post_coalesce_p95 inc >= +15% for 3m or customer_p95_delta >= +7% aggregated over 5m.
  - Collect traces (x-trace-id), KV cache dashboards, and kernel perf flamegraphs.
  - Postmortem template: timeline, metric deltas, root cause, fix, customers impacted, prevention.

Open risks and mitigation:
- Risk: oscillation on bursty traffic causing ripples in p95 — mitigation: cooldown window + per-route inflight ceiling.
- Risk: KV cache incompatibility where coalesced requests diverge in key addressing — mitigation: handshake with kv-cache-seed-id and explicit opt-out.
- Risk: regression from kernel path differences on older CUDA drivers — mitigation: kernel test matrix and disable coalescing if kernel path is not present.

Follow ups / TODOs (owners + rough ETA):
- INF-3421 (Diego) — finalize canary config and gating in Console (ETA: 2026-06-03).
- INF-3478 (Liam) — add per-route inflight quick-reject; include test coverage for race conditions (ETA: 2026-06-04).
- PR #659 (Sara) — clean up kernel buffer pool and add perf test on 4096/8192 seq (ETA: 2026-06-02).
- Add dashboard panels (Anya) — coalesce_* metrics + heatmap of per-model coalesce_compat (ETA: 2026-06-03).
- SRE (oncall rotation) — draft runbook pages for rollback steps and Slack incident playbook (ETA: 2026-06-05).

Small notes / scratchpad (informal):
- Quick hack: a route-level override header (x-rdwd-coalesce-force=1) helped debug a jitter incident; remember to strip in prod path.
- Observed a weird case where function-calls with near-identical prompts got merged and downstream tool-call serializers got confused. Add stronger opt-out for tool-calls.
- Conversation with solutions-eng: we should provide a one-pager for customers explaining how coalescing affects tail latency vs cost.

Appendix: Useful links and logs
- Kernel bench logs: s3://redwood-inference-bench/serving-runtime/2026-05/kernel-coalesce-logs.tar.gz
- Experiment dashboards: Console > Serving Runtime > Adaptive Coalescing Canary (link in linked_artifacts)
- Local repro: docker image rdwd/coalesce-dev:2026-05-27 (use --repro-seed 42)

Notes for next week:
- Tune per-route defaults: lower max-wait for chat-heavy routes, higher for embeddings/async flows.
- Evaluate combining prefix-KV prefill logic with coalescing to reduce redundant prefill work.
- Prepare customer comms draft for when we flip default to opt-in in Console.

Document owner: Priya Menon (reach via Slack @priya).
